title: Grade 9 Social Science — French Revolution & Russian Revolution
description: French Revolution and Russian Revolution and Socialism practice questions
subject: social-science

questions.question: The French Revolution began in the year:
questions.explanation: The French Revolution began in 1789 with the storming of the Bastille on July 14, 1789. This date is still celebrated as Bastille Day in France.

questions.question: The slogan of the French Revolution was:
questions.explanation: Liberté, Égalité, Fraternité (Liberty, Equality, Fraternity) was the motto of the French Revolution and remains the national motto of France today.

questions.question: The Estates-General in France was a representation of which social groups?
options: Church, nobility, and common people (clergy, nobles, Third Estate)
questions.explanation: The Estates-General had three estates: First Estate (clergy), Second Estate (nobility), Third Estate (everyone else — peasants, bourgeoisie). The Third Estate had 97% of the population but little power.

questions.question: The Declaration of the Rights of Man and Citizen (1789) was influenced by ideas of:
options: Enlightenment thinkers like Rousseau and Voltaire
questions.explanation: The Declaration of Rights of Man and Citizen was influenced by Enlightenment ideas — natural rights, equality, liberty — promoted by philosophers like Rousseau, Voltaire, and Montesquieu.

questions.question: The 'Reign of Terror' in France (1793-94) was led by:
questions.explanation: Maximilien Robespierre headed the Committee of Public Safety during the Reign of Terror. About 16,000 people were guillotined, including Robespierre himself in July 1794.

questions.question: Napoleon Bonaparte rose to power in France after:
options: The Revolution weakened and created political instability
questions.explanation: Napoleon exploited the political instability following the Revolution and the Directory's failures. He seized power in the coup of 18 Brumaire (1799) and became First Consul.

questions.question: The storming of the Bastille was significant because:
options: It released many important political prisoners
It symbolised the fall of royal authority and tyranny
It was won by British soldiers
questions.explanation: The Bastille was a royal fortress and prison that symbolised royal tyranny. Its storming on July 14, 1789, symbolised the fall of despotic rule, even though few prisoners were actually inside.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT a cause of the French Revolution?
options: Heavy taxes on the poor and Third Estate
Lavish lifestyle of the royal court
Ideas of liberty and equality from Enlightenment philosophers
questions.explanation: The causes of the French Revolution were financial crisis, social inequality, royal extravagance, and Enlightenment ideas. Britain's prosperity was not a direct cause.

questions.question: The Russian Revolution took place in the year:
questions.explanation: The Russian Revolution occurred in 1917. The February Revolution overthrew Tsar Nicholas II, and the October Revolution brought the Bolsheviks to power under Lenin.

questions.question: The leader of the Bolshevik party who led the October Revolution was:
questions.explanation: Vladimir Ilyich Lenin led the Bolsheviks in the October Revolution of 1917. He had returned from exile in April 1917 and guided the party to overthrow the Provisional Government.

questions.question: Karl Marx's ideology believed that history is driven by:
options: Class struggle between the bourgeoisie (owners) and proletariat (workers)
questions.explanation: Marx's theory of historical materialism: all history is a history of class struggle. The bourgeoisie (capitalist class) exploit the proletariat (working class), eventually leading to revolution.

questions.question: The Soviets in Russia were:
questions.explanation: Soviets were elected councils of workers, soldiers, and peasants that emerged during the 1905 and 1917 revolutions. The Bolsheviks rallied support with the slogan 'All power to the Soviets.'

questions.question: The New Economic Policy (NEP) introduced by Lenin in 1921 allowed:
options: Limited private enterprise to rebuild the economy after war and famine
Foreign companies to take over Russian industries
Peasants to be removed from land
questions.explanation: The NEP was a pragmatic step back — it allowed limited private trade and agriculture to recover the economy after the chaos of WWI, revolution, and Civil War.

questions.question: The event known as 'Bloody Sunday' (1905) refers to:
options: Tsarist troops firing on peaceful protesters in St. Petersburg
The start of World War I
questions.explanation: On January 22, 1905, Tsarist troops fired on peaceful workers marching to petition Tsar Nicholas II. The massacre killed hundreds and sparked the 1905 Revolution.

questions.question: The USSR (Union of Soviet Socialist Republics) was officially formed in:
questions.explanation: The USSR was formally established on December 30, 1922, as a federation of Soviet republics — Russia, Ukraine, Belorussia, and the Transcaucasus.
